summary: WoodStock Grants to support climate-smart wood construction solutions
content: WoodStock Grants to support climate-smart wood construction solutions
citation: Climate-smart use of wood in the construction sector to support the New European Bauhaus. Available at: https://ec.europa.eu/info/funding-tenders/opportunities/portal/screen/opportunities/competitive-calls-cs/45656490
metadata.caName: ['WoodStock Grants to support climate-smart wood construction solutions']
metadata.description:
['

The construction sector is central to Europe\'s climate transition. At the same time, significant volumes of hardwood, residual wood, low-quality wood, and damaged wood remain until today underutilised. Unlocking this potential can reduce waste, strengthen local value chains, and create sustainable economic opportunities. The WoodStock grants support this transition by supporting one-year projects that combine innovation, circularity, and community engagement — embedding the New European Bauhaus (NEB) values of together, sustainable, and beautiful into practical construction solutions.

Funding may be used for one or more of the following activities:

  1. Demonstration: Prototyping, experimental set-up of innovations related to WoodStock.
  2. Testing: Physical and mechanical validation, certification preparation.
  3. Co-creation: Activities with local actors and users to improve the solution and embed them in the local value chain and community.
  4. Training: Workshops to develop new skills and knowledge.
  5. Dissemination: Communication about the solutions to a wide audience (including video production) (max. 20% of total budget).,

Eligible expenses may include equipment, laboratory testing, materials, logistics, multimedia production, and staff costs related to the above-mentioned activities.

Selected projects are expected to:

  1. Develop climate-smart wood construction solutions beyond TRL5.
  2. Jointly organise one co-creation session with a WoodStock Living Lab in the Netherlands, France, Slovenia, Poland, Ireland or Norway.
  3. Document successful and unsuccessful innovation steps they have made, and lessons learned throughout the process.
  4. Share experiences and lessons learned with the WoodStock consortium.
  5. Contribute to the WoodBook and the European Wood Construction Observatory.
  6. Align dissemination with the WoodStock communication partner and contribute to WoodStock communication materials by providing input.

For questions about the call, please contact grants@woodstockproject.eu.

']
metadata.title: ['Climate-smart use of wood in the construction sector to support the New European Bauhaus']

metadata.description:

Expected Innovation Experiments

Applicants will propose an innovation experiment that improves an existing product, service or application using Space-IoT Box resources. The proposed experiment must:

  1. Address a relevant climate-smart agriculture challenge.
  2. Use Copernicus, Earth Observation, IoT or other Space-IoT Box-supported resources.
  3. Demonstrate how the existing product, service or application will be improved.
  4. Present a clear implementation plan, expected outputs and budget.
  5. Show potential value for users, customers or stakeholders in the Lake Victoria Basin region or the wider target countries.

Example Application Areas

Applicants may propose innovation experiments linked to areas such as:

  1. Weather and climate monitoring using IoT sensors and remote sensing data.
  2. Water quality monitoring for fish farming.
  3. Fish farming decision-support services.
  4. Crop monitoring and crop phenology.
  5. Farm input planning, irrigation support and farm management.
  6. Crop disease risk monitoring and alerts.
  7. Seasonal planning and agroclimatic zoning.
  8. Precision agriculture using satellite imagery and IoT data.
  9. Hydrological flow assessment using IoT observations and satellite image analysis.

These are example areas. Applicants may propose other relevant climate-smart agriculture solutions that can benefit from Space-IoT Box resources.

What Selected Applicants Will Receive

Selected SMEs and start-ups will receive:

  1. Access to Space-IoT Box resources, tools, datasets and documentation.
  2. Technical training on relevant Copernicus, Earth Observation and IoT resources.
  3. Business development and entrepreneurial support.
  4. Product and market validation support.
  5. Pitch and investment readiness support.
  6. Mentoring during the innovation experiment implementation period.
  7. Opportunity to present the innovation experiment during the final showcase.
  8. Financial support of up to EUR 5,000 for eligible costs linked to the approved innovation experiment.

summary: ForestPathways – Building Knowledge and Solutions for Resilient Forests and Sustainable Forest-Based Futures
content: ForestPathways – Building Knowledge and Solutions for Resilient Forests and Sustainable Forest-Based Futures
citation: European partnership: Forests and Forestry for a Sustainable Future. Available at: https://ec.europa.eu/info/funding-tenders/opportunities/portal/screen/opportunities/competitive-calls-cs/48213468
metadata.caName: ['ForestPathways – Building Knowledge and Solutions for Resilient Forests and Sustainable Forest-Based Futures']
metadata.description:
['

The FOREST Joint Call 2026 – ForestPathways supports transnational research and innovation activities across the spectrum from fundamental research to applied research and, where appropriate, demonstration activities. Projects are expected to generate new knowledge, develop practical solutions, and contribute to implementation in policy, management or industry contexts, while considering the diversity of forests and the forest-based sector.

Applicants must select the single topic that best reflects the primary focus of their proposal. Proposals may address multiple topics but will be evaluated and ranked under one primary topic.

TOPIC 1 – Climate-Resilient Forest Systems: “How forests function and respond to climate change”

This topic supports research and innovation addressing the resilience, adaptive capacity, and long-term sustainability of forest ecosystems under changing environmental conditions, including climate change and increasing disturbance pressures. It aims to strengthen the scientific basis for climate-resilient forest systems and support their adaptation and mitigation to climate change, within broader environmental and socioeconomic contexts.

Proposals should address, where relevant, carbon dynamics measurement, monitoring and assessment of carbon stocks and sinks; adaptation pathways and strategies; forest ecosystem processes and dynamics; disturbance regimes, including wildfires and other abiotic and biotic disturbances, pests and diseases; landscape-level interactions and spatial dynamics; and genetic diversity and adaptive capacity, including assisted migration.

TOPIC 2 – Adaptive and Multifunctional Forest Management Systems: “How forests should be managed under changing conditions”

This topic supports research and innovation focused on the implementation of adaptive and multifunctional forest management systems that enhance resilience, sustainability, and the provision of multiple ecosystem services. It aims to support forest management approaches capable of responding to ecological change, disturbance risks, and evolving environmental, economic, and societal demands.

Proposals should address, where relevant, silvicultural systems and management approaches supporting resilient and multifunctional forests; sustainable harvesting and wood mobilisation methods; monitoring, assessment and planning tools for adaptive management; integration of forest genetic resources into management strategies; operational, digital and technical innovations; risk reduction and adaptation strategies; and trade-offs and synergies between ecosystem services.

TOPIC 3 – Timber and Innovative Wood-Based Products: “How wood is transformed into innovative products”

This topic supports research and innovation on the development, performance, and uptake of timber and innovative wood-based products contributing to decarbonisation and the circular bioeconomy. It aims to advance the development and market uptake of sustainable wood-based products and systems, supporting the substitution of fossil-based and carbon-intensive materials and contributing to low-carbon construction and manufacturing.

Proposals should address, where relevant, engineered timber and timber construction systems; high-value wood-based products, chemicals and materials; substitution of fossil-based and other carbon-intensive materials; more sustainable alternatives to polluting wood treatments and processing practices; standardisation, testing and certification; circular and resource-efficient use of wood-based products; innovative use of underutilised softwood and hardwood species; innovative manufacturing technologies; and approaches to increase market demand and consumer acceptance and uptake.

TOPIC 4 – Forest Value Chains, Markets and Governance: “How forest-based sectors, markets and governance are organised”

This topic supports research and innovation strengthening the resilience, sustainability, and functioning of forest-based value chains, markets, and governance systems, supporting the transition towards a sustainable and circular forest-based bioeconomy. It aims to support resilient, sustainable, competitive, and innovative forest-based value chains and governance systems capable of responding to environmental, economic, and societal transitions.

Proposals should address, where relevant, forest-based value chains and market organisation; innovative business models, economic viability and investment readiness; policy, regulatory and governance instruments; barriers to market uptake and innovation deployment; cascading use, circularity and efficient resource use; skills, labour, education and workforce development; and European resilience in sustainable raw material supply, value chains, local processing capacities and forest-based economies.

The topics provide strategic direction and facilitate evaluation. They are not exhaustive and do not restrict the submission of innovative or cross-cutting proposals aligned with the overall objectives of the call.

']
metadata.title: ['European partnership: Forests and Forestry for a Sustainable Future']

summary: EIT Regional Innovation Booster Hungary 2027
content: EIT Regional Innovation Booster Hungary 2027
citation: Cross-KIC EIT Regional Innovation & Internationalisation Business Plan 2026. Available at: https://ec.europa.eu/info/funding-tenders/opportunities/portal/screen/opportunities/competitive-calls-cs/48939690
metadata.description:
['

The EIT Regional Innovation Booster (EIT RIB) Hungary seven-month international market-access programme for Hungarian start-ups.

With the support of the Hungarian National Innovation Agency, it supports mature, innovation-driven Hungarian companies to validate, enter and grow in a new European market. A single cohort of 8 companies will be selected and equipped with a validated market entry strategy, concrete connections in their target market, and the operational know-how to act on them. 

At the heart of the programme is a Buddy system that pairs each company with an experienced operator who already knows the chosen target market and sector. This is complemented by expert mentoring, a programme of workshops and guest speaker sessions, and a EUR 2.500 conference and travel grant to support in-person engagement in the target market. 

The programme runs from December 2026 to June 2027 and is structured in two consecutive phases. 

Phase 1: Market Preparation (Months 1–3) Selected companies validate their target market with 20 hours of 1:1 expert mentoring, assess their readiness for international expansion, and build an executable market entry strategy.  

Phase 2: Market Expansion (Months 4–7) Each company works up to 40 hours with its matched EIT RIB Buddy to start entering the chosen target market, supported by continued workshops and guest speakers, international matchmaking, and optional participation in EIT Community events. 

To be eligible, applicants must: 

-Be a for-profit SME (according to the EU definition) registered in Hungary

-Have at least 3 full-time employees (FTEs) at the time of application

-Hold full ownership of, or exclusive commercialisation rights to, the intellectual property behind the solution to be taken abroad

-Have a novel product, service, technology or deep tech solution with demonstrated product-market fit in Hungary and proven commercial traction

-Operate in one of the EIT thematic areas: Climate, Digital, Food & Agritech, Healthcare, Energy and Renewables, Raw Materials, Urban Mobility, or Culture & Creativity.

']

summary: AENAON Open Call 1
content: AENAON Open Call 1
citation: Preparedness Support and Mutual Assistance, Targeting Larger Industrial Operations and Installations. Available at: https://ec.europa.eu/info/funding-tenders/opportunities/portal/screen/opportunities/competitive-calls-cs/47039365
metadata.description:
['

Basic information

AENAON implements two competitive Open Call rounds through its Financial Support to Third Parties (FSTP) scheme. The Open Calls aim to maximise the uptake, integration, testing and validation of AENAON technologies and services, including the Federated Digital Twin-based Cyber Range Platform, cybersecurity training capabilities and cybersecurity preparedness services, in realistic offshore wind and related critical-infrastructure environments.

The Open Calls are designed to engage SMEs and start-ups, large enterprises and technology providers, research organisations and universities, cybersecurity service and technology providers, offshore wind operators, manufacturers and supply-chain actors, energy and critical-infrastructure stakeholders, and other relevant innovation actors. Supported third-party projects are expected to contribute practical use cases, validation evidence, technical feedback and sector-relevant results that strengthen the cybersecurity and resilience of the offshore wind ecosystem.

Open Call 1 focuses on the initial validation, integration and testing of AENAON technologies and services in realistic environments. Activities may include the development and validation of sector-specific cybersecurity scenarios, identification and assessment of offshore-wind-relevant vulnerabilities, integration with simulation and cyber range environments, cybersecurity testing and training activities, and validation of cybersecurity tools, services and preparedness capabilities.

Open Call 1 sub-projects are expected to have an implementation period of 8 months, with clearly defined tasks, milestones, deliverables, KPIs and acceptance evidence.

Applicants may propose activities related to cybersecurity testing and validation, cyber range training and scenario-based exercises, vulnerability assessment, penetration testing, threat and risk assessment, risk monitoring, cyberattack management, digital twin-based validation and integration, or other cybersecurity resilience use cases that are demonstrably aligned with the objectives and technical capabilities of AENAON.

Budget

The total AENAON FSTP budget is €4,100,000.

The indicative allocation is:

  1. €2,100,000 for Open Call 1
  2. €2,000,000 for Open Call 2

Any amount not committed under Open Call 1 may be reallocated to Open Call 2, subject to budget availability, the applicable Open Call rules and the principles of transparency, equal treatment and sound financial management.

Funding Constraints

AENAON will provide sub-grants under two Open Calls (Open Call 1 and 2), with a total FSTP allocation of €4,100,000. In line with the call topic, the scheme derogates from the €60k ceiling, allowing up to €100,000 per individual third party (only in the case of offshore wind farm operators and manufacturers, which are considered large critical infrastructures/ operators of essential services) and up to €150,000 per action (in case of small consortia).

Example 1 — SME A, Open Call 1

  1. Entity A is a generic SME, applicable ceiling: €60,000
  2. Funding requested/awarded in Open Call 1: €55,000
  3. Result: Eligible (Remaining funding capacity for Open Call 2 under AENAON: €5,000, if applicable)

Example 2 — Offshore wind-farm operator B, Open Call 1

  1. Entity B is an offshore wind-farm operator and therefore benefits from the derogated ceiling; applicable ceiling: €100,000
  2. Funding awarded in Open Call 1: €87,000
  3. Result: Eligible (Remaining funding capacity for Open Call 2: €13,000, if applicable)

Example 3 — Small consortium B + C, Open Call 2

  1. In Open Call 2, B and C form a small consortium. B = offshore wind-farm operator/manufacturer, and C = SME, thus, maximum funding per consortium action: €150,000.
  2. However, the individual ceilings must also be respected. Since B already received €87,000 in Open Call 1, B can receive only €100,000 − €87,000 = €13,000
  3. C has received no previous AENAON funding. Therefore, C can receive up to €60,000
  4. The total maximum eligible AENAON funding for the consortium (B+C) in Open Call 2 is therefore €73,000 (B up to €13,000, C up to €60,000)
  5. Consortium action (budget requested): €73k < €150k maximum per action

The final lump-sum amount awarded to each selected third-party beneficiary will be fixed at the contracting stage through a needs-based, auditable right-sizing process, taking into account the proposed activities, technical complexity, budget needs, expected contribution to AENAON objectives, evaluation outcome, milestones, deliverables, and acceptance criteria.

Payment Schedule

AENAON applies a staged payment model of 30% – 40% – 30%:

  1. 30% initial payment upon signature of the Sub-Grant Agreement and completion of onboarding requirements
  2. 40% interim payment following successful completion of the mid-term review and acceptance of required interim reports, deliverables and supporting evidence
  3. 30% final payment following completion of the action and acceptance of the final report, final deliverables, performance evidence and required outputs

Payments are conditional upon the satisfactory achievement of agreed milestones, deliverables and acceptance criteria. Payments may be suspended, reduced or recovered in cases of non-performance, breach of contractual obligations, false declarations, conflict of interest, ineligible activities or serious non-compliance with reporting, ethics, GDPR, visibility or audit requirements.

']
metadata.title: ['Preparedness Support and Mutual Assistance, Targeting Larger Industrial Operations and Installations']

metadata.description:
['

The scope of the I3FLOAT 1st Open Call is to fund SMEs with proposed innovations in the field of Floating Offshore Wind and proposing a technological solution to one of the challenges posed by the I3FLOAT project. The support scheme aims to fund projects that are relatively close to commercialisation. The expected current TRLs for projects funded under the support scheme are TRL 6-8.

Applicants to the 1st Open Call should propose a project that is in line with the different challenges the I3FLOAT project has identified. These challenges can be Open Challenges, which means solutions that are aligned with any of the innovation lines prioritised in the Strategic Innovation Agenda, or Specific Challenges, more concrete and defined by a Challenge Owner.

Open Challenges refers to innovations that are aligned with the 44 prioritised innovation lines identified in the Floating Wind Strategic Innovation Agenda in areas such as Floating substructures, mooring systems and dynamic cables; Electrical infrastructure and grid connection; Wind turbine, tower or alternative supporting structures and FOW-specific control; Industrialisation; Logistics and offshore installation; Operation, Maintenance and Decommissioning. Further detail is available in the Annex 1 of the Submission Toolkit.

Specific Challenges are related to specific sectoral needs proposed by so-called Challenge Owners. Examples would be the challenge "Single-pass welding outside for local FOWT serial assembly" proposed by I3FLOAT partner Eolink or "Logistic optimization on the transport of offshore wind structures" proposed by I3 Board member Navantia Seanergies. The list of the 11 Specific Challenges is available in Annex 2 of the Submission Toolkit.

metadata.description:
['

Open data about software packages is critical for the automation and scale necessary to resolve software supply chain management and address security and regulatory and open source compliance challenges. CodeSupply aggregates and curates comprehensive software metadata, including origin and licensing information, security vulnerabilities, and quality metrics from distributed, authoritative data sources across programming ecosystems and software types. This metadata is assembled in reference data sets, federated in a unified data catalog for digital sovereignty and independence, and distributed as open data, freely available to all, using an open source data license.


The CodeSupply project pursues three interconnected objectives that directly address data challenges in cybersecurity, software supply chain management, and regulatory and open source license compliance:

  1. Publish current, correct, and comprehensive software metadata
  2. Establish a scalable and sustainable mechanism to provide democratic access to data sets
  3. Create a foundational framework for future iterations, enhancements, and new data sets


CodeSupply will deliver an ambitious development effort, but this is a vast domain with many more challenges than what any preconceived effort could tackle by itself. This is why we invite your contribution to help us reshape the state of play, and together create an open, trustworthy and reliable internet for all.


This is your opportunity to make a real difference. You tell us how your project can help CodeSupply go harder, better, faster, stronger. In order to enable you to make such contributions, we will award small to medium-size R&D grants towards solutions that bring the next generation of mobile solutions closer. We are seeking project proposals between 5.000 and 50.000 euro\'s — which should get you on your way. If the project works out well you can subsequently scale up in other programmes funded by NLnet such as Restack. Noteworthy fact: several projects within CodeSupply were themselves bootstrapped on precisely such a grant from NLnet, and now it is your turn.

']

metadata.description:
['

Open Internet Stack is an initiative by the European Commission to work towards an resilient operational stack of strategic technology commons worthy of trust — a stable and defendable foundation to foster healthy and strong democracies and economies, delivering the European vision of next generation digital infrastructures and connected collaborative computing networks. It aims to deliver an ecosystem of deployable, scalable, and secure technologies that allow for permissionless innovation, contribute to quality of life and deliver strategic autonomy.


The goal of Restack is to help deliver, mature and scale new internet commons across the technology stack: from libre chips to middleware without a vendor lock-in, from productivity tools to \'local-first\' infrastructure — and of course the end user applications needed to consume those networked services. We restack because there is no other viable way. If we want to reclaim digital self-sustainability and yield the full benefits from technology as a society, we need to have an entire stack that is open from the ground up — period.


Only though enough critical mass of shared building blocks and collective pooling of resources and capabilities will our governments, businesses and civil society be able to count on digital security and long term operational availability — and steer towards more fair, innovative economies and societies. And there is no time to waste. This is why we invite your contribution to help us reshape the state of play, and together create an open, trustworthy and reliable internet for all.


This is your opportunity to make a real difference. In order to enable you to make such contributions, we will award small to medium-size R&D grants towards solutions that bring the next generation of mobile solutions closer. We are seeking project proposals between 5.000 and 50.000 euro\'s — which should get you on your way. if there is proven potential, there is a possibility to subsequently scale up your project significantly. Next to financial support, we provide all kinds of help too — ranging from accessiibility scans and security audits to reproducible packaging, and from support with copyright compliance and governance to standardisation.

']

Our 3-year Regenerative Grazing Programme is designed to help farmers improve their farm\'s soil and environment by changing how their animals feed on the land (so-called "adaptive livestock management"). By joining this Regenerative Grazing Programme, farmers will become part of a local network of farmers and experts where they can share ideas, compare results, and learn from each other\'s experiences.

The overall objective of the Programme is to encourage Farmers to actively engage in regenerative farming, through simplicity, continuous guidance, access to finance & business consultation and data-driven communication.

The main activity expected from the Farming Projects is the implementation of Regenerative Livestock Grazing Practices based on regional farming realities and contexts.

Other activities:

  1. Soil health assessment.
  2. Pervasive soil health monitoring using sensors.
  3. Animal welfare assessment.
  4. Environmental performance assessment (Environmental Life Cycle Assessment\ufffeELCA).
  5. Social impact assessment.
  6. Sharing expertise, ideas exchange, and RLGPs co-design.


The Programme is divided into 3 main stages over the 36 months. Farmers will receive their grant in installments upon the successful completion of each stage.

summary: NetZeroCities ECT2: Enabling City Transformation 2
content: NetZeroCities ECT2: Enabling City Transformation 2
citation: Specific Grant Agreement to the FPA to reinforce the operations of the Climate-Neutral and Smart Cities Mission Platform. Available at: https://ec.europa.eu/info/funding-tenders/opportunities/portal/screen/opportunities/competitive-calls-cs/48400288
metadata.description:
['

ECT2 will expand the existing portfolio of whole-city transformation activities and interventions by focusing on implementation barriers shared by cities across the Mission.

The core shift introduced in this call is a move away from broad, domain-based support towards a more focused model that organises action around clearly defined systemic barriers and bottlenecks.

To this end, ECT2 is organised around six challenge areas which represent critical city-wide implementation barriers that currently prevent cities from translating Climate City Contract ambitions into replicable and scalable outcomes.

The challenge areas are:

  1. Place-based heating and cooling
  2. Nature Based Solutions at city scale
  3. Urban energy systems
  4. City finance innovation for climate neutrality
  5. Large-scale building retrofits and renovations
  6. Decarbonising urban mobility and logistics

All applicants must:

  1. Choose the challenge area that resonates most and anchor the rationale for intervention within this area.
  2. Within their chosen challenge area, formulate an adequate context-specific impact pathway following the impact framework. While the impact pathway describes how the proposed intervention is expected to create change, the Impact Framework provides the progression from problem to impact and the structure for how that change will be monitored, evidenced and reported.


Across all challenge areas, ECT2 aims to enable cities to move from constrained implementation to durable, city-wide transformation by combining activities which remove diagnosed systemic blockers and accelerate progress to climate neutrality. To this end, the programme aims to ensure that Mission Cities can:

  1. Deploy and scale climate‑neutral solutions by addressing institutional, policy, financial, governance, market or social bottlenecks that limit uptake or speed.
  2. Translate research, innovation and evidence into operational policy and delivery systems, ensuring that scientific and technical knowledge is effectively embedded into city decision‑making.
  3. Strengthen city capacities and capabilities so that climate‑neutral delivery becomes business‑as‑usual, independent of individual champions or one‑off projects.
  4. Cover a broad range of levers for change (policy, green technology, finance, governance, behavioural change, social innovation, multi-actor collaboration, procurement, new business models as circular economy, etc.)
  5. Enable collaborative governance and citizen engagement models that support systemic, cross‑sectoral climate action and deliver just transition outcomes.


The selection of proposals will result in multiple implementation-enabling innovations focussing on resolving key implementation challenges. Interventions will work individually and in combinations/clusters to generate resolutions for shared barriers.


Activities eligible for funding are:

Interventions should consist of the following activities to be eligible for funding:

  1. Pioneering Activities: Activities that adapt, test or deploy innovative or enabling solutions at city level.
  2. Systemic, Science‑based Innovative Initiatives: Activities that strengthen the connection between research, evidence and city delivery.
  3. Capacity and capability‑building activities: Activities that establish new knowledge, skills and institutional competence within city administrations and key local actors.
  4. Collaborative governance and community‑building activities: Activities that build more collaborative, inclusive and systemic governance arrangements.


Please note: proposed interventions may cover several or all of these descriptions of eligible activities – this list is intended to allow for flexibility in proposing interventions, rather than limiting proposed interventions to any one eligible activity alone.

Applicants will be requested at the point of submitting a proposal to describe and declare the links between their proposed interventions and the eligible activities as listed above.


For more information please refer to the Call Guidelines, which provide information on the aim, scope, and approach of the call and clarify how to submit a proposal, budget requirements, and the review mechanism and decision-making process.

']

content: Financial Support to Startups and Scaleups (Shape Accelerator & Scale Post-Accelerator)
citation: EITCULTURE Business Plan 2026. Available at: https://ec.europa.eu/info/funding-tenders/opportunities/portal/screen/opportunities/competitive-calls-cs/48939704
metadata.caName: ['Financial Support to Startups and Scaleups (Shape Accelerator & Scale Post-Accelerator)']
metadata.description:
['

This call provides financial support and structured growth support to startups and scaleups with high growth potential operating in the Cultural and Creative Sectors and Industries (CCSI). It targets ventures developing tech-enabled, market-driven, and IP-leveraged solutions capable of scaling commercially, generating economic and societal value, and strengthening the competitiveness of Europe’s creative economy. Through a single application process, companies may access different funding and support depending on their stage of development and investment readiness.

Financial Support to Growth-stage Ventures (Shape Acceleration Programme) is designed for early-stage startups that have validated an initial market need and are beginning to generate traction, revenues, or pilot customers, but still require support to strengthen product-market fit, refine their business model, and prepare for larger-scale commercial growth and future investment. Selected ventures may receive initial financial support of up to EUR 100,000, complemented by structured business development, mentoring and investment-readiness support through the EIT Culture & Creativity Shape Acceleration Programme. During the programme’s Demo Day, up to four Shape ventures may be selected to receive additional financial support of up to EUR 100,000, subject to the conditions specified in the Call Guidelines.

Financial Support to Scaling-stage Ventures (Scale Post-Acceleration Programme) targets mature startups and scale-ups that have already demonstrated strong product-market fit, recurring revenues, customer growth, and international scaling potential, and are now seeking to accelerate expansion through external investment and market scaling. Selected ventures may receive financial support of up to EUR 200,000 for non-RIS-based ventures and eligible ventures already included in the EIT Culture & Creativity 100-to-Watch portfolio, or up to EUR 500,000 for eligible RIS-based ventures.

This call is open to legal entities established in EU Member States and Horizon Europe Associated Countries.

']

citation: Cross KIC EIT Innovation & Business Creation Business Plan 2026. Available at: https://ec.europa.eu/info/funding-tenders/opportunities/portal/screen/opportunities/competitive-calls-cs/48939740
metadata.description:
['

The EIT Community New European Bauhaus, led by EIT Urban Mobility in collaboration with EIT Food and Climate KIC, supports local innovation, citizen engagement, entrepreneurship and place-based transformation across Europe.  Through this open call, the EIT Community NEB aims to support two complementary types of local impact: 

Connect NEB is a mono-beneficiary programme that supports community-led initiatives to test new ideas, activate local communities, and experiment with participatory approaches, living labs and new forms of governance inspired by the New European Bauhaus. 

Co-create NEB is a multi-beneficiary programme that supports partnerships between communities, municipalities and other local actors to deliver visible, place-based transformation in public spaces. Proposals must be submitted by a consortium with 2 to 4 members, and at least one must be a city, a region, or an entity affiliated with a city or region.

Both programmes, each with a maximum duration of 10 months, contribute to improving the quality of life of local communities and the environments of the neighbourhoods where they are implemented, taking into account the relevance of each specific local context and valuing the innovation capacity and creativity of each community.

Despite these differences, proposals for both programmes must serve the purpose of achieving the three inseparable core values of the New European Bauhaus: Sustainable (from climate goals, to circularity, zero pollution, and biodiversity), Beautiful (quality of experience and style, beyond functionality) and Together ( from valuing diversity to equality for all, accessibility and affordability).

This Call for Proposals is open to all legal entities established in Member States of the European Union, and/or in Third countries associated to Horizon Europe. Applications from the Regional Innovation Scheme (RIS) countries are encouraged.

Applications must be submitted separately for each programme, as they are subject to different eligibility criteria, target different audiences. Applicants may apply to one or both programmes but can be eligible as the Lead Partner for only one programme.

']

Every selected project must execute a mandatory work plan divided into specific tasks over three programmatic phases: Project Definition (Months 1–2), Project Implementation (Months 3–6), and Project Evaluation (Months 7–9).

Core tasks across these phases include:

  1. Developing a localised baseline assessment, regional water basin characterisation, and local stakeholder mapping database.
  2. Executing targeted regional monitoring activities from the designated catalogue, focusing on flow monitoring, sediment quantity monitoring, and/or rapid ecotoxicological sediment quality assessments.
  3. Conducting active community stakeholder engagement, multi-actor feedback sessions, and environmental awareness campaigns to co-design future measure protocols.
  4. Formulating a comprehensive Regional Strategic Action Plan and Implementation Roadmap with indicative budgets and local timelines to upscale and replicate sustainable practices across other EU basins.

Technical Mentoring Support

Throughout the entire nine-month duration, selected associated regions will receive dedicated, direct technical support from assigned technical partners and project mentors. This provision includes up to eight (8) hours of individual technical mentoring per month per funded project. Mentors will work closely with your local team from the onboarding phase to co-define your project specifications, establish your individual budget and indicators, monitor your practical pilot implementation progress, and facilitate cross-border data harmonisation with the wider consortium network.


']

metadata.caName: ['Community Grant – Citizen Solutions to Sustainability Challenges']
metadata.description:
['

Community grants can be awarded for activities that support the objectives of the Urban Prosumers project and produce one or more of the following results:

  1. Practices, services or models related to sustainable mobility, energy and/or food that benefit people or communities in Tampere
  2. Technological innovations that enable people to both produce and use sustainable solutions
  3. New funding models for communities’ climate actions
  4. New operating models for residents’ participation in the production and use of sustainable solutions
  5. New information on what prevents or enables people’s participation in the production and use of sustainable solutions
  6. New forms of cooperation for climate actions between residents and local actors
  7. Business opportunities and ideas for the Tampere region related to sustainable mobility, energy or food


The sustainability solutions to be funded can be implemented in different forms, such as new services that support sustainable mobility, energy and/or the food economy, digital applications, civic education models and training materials, and the development of forms of cooperation between residents and the City of Tampere.


Please note that the solutions and experiments implemented during the funded community projects must take place in Tampere or focus on Tampere. The aim is that community projects benefit a wider group of people than the applicant’s own community.

']

summary: MANTRA Second Open Call for Manufacturing SMEs
content: MANTRA Second Open Call for Manufacturing SMEs
citation: 'Innovate to transform' support for SME's sustainability transition (CSA). Available at: https://ec.europa.eu/info/funding-tenders/opportunities/portal/screen/opportunities/competitive-calls-cs/45705096
metadata.caName: ['MANTRA Second Open Call for Manufacturing SMEs']
metadata.description:
['

The objective of this call is to select up to 25 manufacturing SMEs that will receive support to define and implement their MANTRA Journey plan, with the aim of becoming more sustainable and innovative.

Through this initiative, selected SMEs will enhance their capacity to adopt advanced technologies and social innovation for sustainability through collaboration with technology providers and by accessing services provided by EU specialised business support networks and organisations. Financial support of up to EUR 50,000 per SME will be available to implement the recommended transformation roadmap following the advisory phase.

Proposals should focus on a transformation project that is realistic, impactful and embedded in the SME’s strategy for long-term sustainability and growth through the uptake of advanced technologies. The proposed concept must contribute to the green and digital transformation of the SME by reducing environmental impacts while enhancing the competitiveness and resilience of the business. Projects should align with circular economy principles and consider inclusive and socially responsible practices.

Selected SMEs will participate in the MANTRA Journey, consisting of a six-month advisory phase followed by a six-month implementation phase supported through MANTRA financial assistance.

Your journey begins by joining the MANTRA Community, which serves as your gateway to resources, peer learning, networking opportunities and access to the application process.

']
metadata.title: ["'Innovate to transform' support for SME's sustainability transition (CSA)"]

metadata.description:
['

The procedure follows the principles of:

  1. transparency,
  2. equal treatment,
  3. confidentiality,
  4. absence of conflict of interest.

Admissibility and eligibility checks precede scoring; only eligible applications will be scored.

Eligible proposals are ranked by total score within the available budget.

The final award decision is endorsed by POLI.design. All applicants will receive a written justification for the decision, with terms to appeal.

Selected beneficiaries will be requested to sign a Financial Support Agreement specifying the supported activity, eligible costs, maximum amount, payment schedule and reporting obligations.

Failure to sign within the indicated timeframe may lead to loss of the grant by the autonomous decision of POLI.design.

Payments will be made by POLI.design, normally after participation in the activity and approval of the beneficiary report and cost statement. Details are provided in the individual Financial Support Agreement (including e.g. the possibility of small prefinancing in justified cases).

']

summary: Open Call for innovative projects enhancing the valorisation of agri-food biomass side-streams
content: Open Call for innovative projects enhancing the valorisation of agri-food biomass side-streams
citation: Joint Cluster Initiatives (EUROCLUSTERS) for Europe’s recovery. Available at: https://ec.europa.eu/info/funding-tenders/opportunities/portal/screen/opportunities/competitive-calls-cs/47108154
metadata.caName: ['Open Call for innovative projects enhancing the valorisation of agri-food biomass side-streams']
metadata.description:
['

This call targets innovative SMEs developing solutions that increase the valorisation of biomass side-streams, contributing to more sustainable and resilient agri-food ecosystems through the development of new processes, services and products.

This Innovation Call includes financial support for projects especially focusing on the development, adoption, and commercialisation of innovative upcycled ingredients for food and non-food applications, products, business processes, and technologies (including digital) that maximise the valorisation of agri-food biomass and side-streams. These projects should have a minimum Technology Readiness Level (TRL) of 6.

1.The Innovation Open Call targets:

  1. SMEs in the agri-food production and/or processing sector;
  2. SMEs in other sectors (ex. cosmetics, nutraceuticals, etc) that valorise biomass/by-products/side-streams from the agri-food sector;
  3. SMEs in other sectors (ex. cosmetics, nutraceuticals, etc) that valorise their own biomass/by-products/side-streams for the agri-food sector;
  4. SMEs offering solutions and/or technology for the valorisation of biomass/by-products/side-streams from the agri-food sector (development and application of new technologies or processes).

2.The applicant’s project must lead to the implementation of either a new process, a new product, or a new service or a combination of them.

3.Proposals can be submitted either by a single SME or by an SMEs consortium with up to three (3) SMEs.

4.Applicants can be SMEs registered at EU Member States and countries associated to the Single Market Programme.

5.Projects must have a minimum Technology Readiness Level (TRL) of at least 6.

6.For Single SME projects, the maximum lump-sum grant per project (1 SME) is €60.000.

7.For collaborative projects, the maximum lump-sum grant per project (2-3 SMEs) is €90.000.

8.Innovation grants must be matched by at least 15% private financial contribution (debt or own financial resources), with proof required.


AMENDMENT 16 JULY 2026

Following aspects of the call text have been updated and clarified:

  1. Thematic priorities - scope of the call and valorisation pathways
  2. Call definitions: biosolutions added, TRL requirements clarified
  3. Documents required: no stamp needed, only signature
  4. Eligibility criteria
  5. Evaluation procedure, criteria and scoring: 2 stage evaluation process in Cut-off 2, pre-selection (knock-out stage) added. Timing of the evaluation procedure cut-off 2 prolonged
  6. Re-submission of proposals: to be done in new application form
  7. Period to file complaints
  8. SPOC contact details

Pay attention that there is an adapted application form for cut-off 2!

']
metadata.title: ['Joint Cluster Initiatives (EUROCLUSTERS) for Europe’s recovery']

content: Enhancing the Cybersecurity Capabilities of the Domestic SME Sector (SSNS-NCC-HU-FSTP-2026)
citation: Deploying The Network of National Coordination Centres with Member States. Available at: https://ec.europa.eu/info/funding-tenders/opportunities/portal/screen/opportunities/competitive-calls-cs/46786367
metadata.caName: ['Enhancing the Cybersecurity Capabilities of the Domestic SME Sector (SSNS-NCC-HU-FSTP-2026)']
metadata.description:
['

WHO CAN SUBMIT A GRANT APPLICATION?

Micro, small and medium-sized enterprises may submit grant applications for the call if they:

  1. have at least three closed financial years (each supported by financial statements and covering full 365-day period of operation as a pre-company is not included);
  2. operate in the sectors listed in Annexes 2 or 3 of the Cybersecurity Act

WHAT ACTIVITIES ARE ELIGIBLE FOR SUPPORT?

  1. Acquisition of new equipment and intangible assets resulting in the enhancement of cyber resilience
  2. Centralised endpoint protection solutions (traditional antivirus);
  3. Advanced endpoint protection and incident detection solutions (EDR/XDR);
  4. Perimeter protection solutions (firewall, Web Application Firewall, proxy, VPN gateway);
  5. Network traffic monitoring and intrusion detection solutions (WAF, IDS/IPS, NDR);
  6. Solutions against denial-of-service attacks (Anti-DDoS);
  7. Data backup and recovery solutions (backup/restore);
  8. Centralised log collection solutions (log management);
  9. Advanced log analysis solutions;
  10. Security information and event management solutions (SIEM);
  11. Mobile device management solutions (MDM);
  12. Multi-factor authentication solutions (MFA);
  13. Identity and access a management solutions (IAM);
  14. Data loss prevention solutions (DLP);
  15. Anti-spam and e-mail security solutions;
  16. Governance, risk and compliance management solutions (GRC);
  17. Encryption and key management solutions;
  18. Replacement of hardware or software components that are no longer supported by security update (obsolete hardware/software).
  19. Procurement of Services related to the enhancement of cyber resilience:
  20. Cybersecurity testing and assessment services (vulnerability testing);
  21. Cybersecurity Operations Centre (SOC) services;
  22. Cybersecurity-related training activities;
  23. Subscriptions to cybersecurity training platforms;
  24. Integration of hardware and software tools (system design, implementation, configuration, testing and documentation);
  25. Cybersecurity-related consulting and professional advisory services.

Details are included in the call for tenders!

']

summary: FuseNet Support of Master Students going on an internship abroad
content: FuseNet Support of Master Students going on an internship abroad
citation: Euratom-Adhoc-2021-2027. Available at: https://ec.europa.eu/info/funding-tenders/opportunities/portal/screen/opportunities/competitive-calls-cs/43549596
metadata.caName: ['FuseNet Support of Master Students going on an internship abroad']
metadata.description:
['

This support package is meant to facilitate MSc students in fusion who want to go abroad for an internship, thereby stimulating quality of education through exchanges. The internship can take place at a fusion research centre or university involved in fusion research. This place is not limited to Europe. Students registered at universities that are a FuseNet member and/or are doing their internship at hosts that are a FuseNet member, and their home university is located in one of the EUROfusion member states can apply for financial support for their internship here.

The financial support consists of a fixed amount of travel support (depending on the travel distance) and accommodation/living support (depending on the internship duration). The application has to be submitted at least 2 weeks before and within 6 months of the start of the internship. metadata.description:
['

About Phortify

Phortify - Photonics Education Network for Next-Gen Innovation and Digital Skills Excellence for Industry and Society - is dedicated to the Enhancement and Harmonisation of Photonics education and training across Europe. Phortify offers a two-year European Master’s in Photonics Engineering, combining advanced coursework, hands-on laboratory training, and cutting-edge digital skills development, structured mobility windows and industry placements. Students who complete the Phortify track receive an official Phortify Certificate in addition to their Master’s degree. Students can enrol in a Phortify-related master programme at any of the 7 participating universities. In addition, Phortify provides stand-alone modules with harmonised standards for quality assurance and certification, offering high flexibility and mobility for both students and industry professionals. Finally, Phortify organises mentoring programmes for women postdocs and early PIs as well as one-day immersive experience events for prospective students, providing a unique opportunity to explore photonics and its applications.

About the Phortify Funding Framework

Phortify’s Funding Framework aims to widen participation in photonics by supporting students and staff who are traditionally underrepresented in STEM. This includes women and gender minorities, students from low-income or socio-economically disadvantaged backgrounds, first-generation university students, and learners with disabilities or specific support needs. The programme also encourages participation from regions with limited access to advanced higher education, as well as those belonging to cultural or minority groups that may be underrepresented in higher education. By addressing these dimensions of diversity, Phortify helps ensure a more inclusive and equitable community of future photonics professionals. Participants selected for Phortify funding receive financial support for studies and mobility pathways within the participating master programmes, or for mentoring programmes and STEM experience workshops organised by one of the Phortify partners.

']
metadata.title: ['Specialised Education Programmes in Key Capacity Areas']
